messages:
sylvia: quick thread  following the ingestion-rfc, I prototyped two approaches for cost attribution when enrichment can be async: 1) inline compact headers, 2) small provenance envelope referenced by id. posting pros/cons and a strawman.

ram: TL;DR please — which wins for us on latency and billing accuracy?

sylvia: short: envelope wins for accuracy and versioning, headers win for simplicity/latency. tradeoffs: envelope needs an extra lookup for billing/recon jobs; headers increase header size and risk high-cardinality metrics.

oscar: can you enumerate the failure modes? e.g., lost provenance blob, stale mapping table, header rewrite during proxying.

sylvia: great Q. failure modes: 1) blob missing -> fallback to cost_key header if present; 2) header mutated by intermediate (bad) -> we detect via provenance_checksum in envelope; 3) mapping service lag -> use cost_key_v default mapping to 'unknown' bucket for short window.

nia: about header size: we worry about per-request TCP/HTTP overhead and client SDK compatibility. Instead of free-form comma paths, consider a compact, base64-encoded protobuf with fixed fields: origin_id(2b), route_id(2b), model_id(hash16). that keeps header under ~64 bytes usually.\

ram: protobuf header is interesting. but opaque blobs hinder ops (human debugging). we need a readable prefix or well-known decode tool in logs.

sylvia: agree — plan: header has two parts: a short human-readable cost_key and a compact envelope_ref. header schema: X-Cost-Key (readable), X-Prov-Ref (p-xxxx). ingest paths should rely on X-Cost-Key for fast routing, reconciliations use X-Prov-Ref -> envelope blob.

oscar: and for sampling? if traces are sampled out upstream we might never see the enrichment that adds tenant info. do we accept a best-effort recon once enrich finishes?

sylvia: yes. reconciliation job will subscribe to enrich-complete events and attempt to reconcile any sampled traces used for billing. rules: envelope wins; cost_key immutable at ingest. enrichers must post envelope with provenance_id if they add attribution hints.

ram: operational constraints: how long to retain envelopes? SLOs for envelope-store reads?

ia: infra-bot: note: envelope-store implementation options: S3 + index, Redis cache for hot reads, or Dynamo + S3 for cold. recommended retention: 60 days for billing, 14 days hot cache.

sylvia: suggested SLA: envelope-store read 99.95 for hot cache, 99.9 for cold within 200ms median. mapping service read 99.95 (reads during aggregation). writes are eventual; migrations coordinate via mapping-v tags in envelope.

oscar: metrics impact: if we tag metrics at ingest with raw cost_key, we'll explode cardinality when cost_key_v changes or when model hashes differ. propose two-tier tags: stable_key (tenant+route), detail_key (model, variant) only for flamegraphs/trace-level. aggregation pipeline can join stable_key -> product lines.

nia: implement derivation rules as a config: stable_keys = [tenant, route], detailed_keys = [model, variant, quant]. default sampler drops detailed tags for metrics.

ram: reconcile with historical billing: mapping service needs time-travel queries (map cost_key at T to canonical bucket). that's extra complexity. we should version-mutate cost_key only through a controlled migration service that emits mapping events.

sylvia: yep strawman: provide cost_key_v and mapping_id in envelope. mapping service stores effective_bucket for (cost_key, cost_key_v, effective_time). aggregation reads mapping as of event time.

oscar: sample header/envelope example please.

sylvia: snippet:

```
HTTP headers:
X-Trace-Id: 0af3c2
X-Cost-Key: tenant=acme|route=chat
X-Prov-Ref: p-1f8b (optional compact ref)
X-Cost-Key-V: 3

Envelope (p-1f8b) contents (stored in envelope-store):
{ "prov_id": "p-1f8b", "trace_id": "0af3c2", "full_path": ["edge-1","proxy-a","enr-09"], "cost_key": "tenant=acme|route=chat|model=gptq-v3", "cost_key_v": 3, "mapping_id": "map-2026-01", "checksum": "sha256:..." }
```

nia: a couple of implementation notes: 1) use a short prov_ref namespace to avoid long headers (p- hex), 2) sign/encrypt envelopes when they contain PII, 3) index by prov_id and trace_id for quick lookup.

ram: action items: sylvia + nia to draft envelope proto and retention plan; oscar to propose metric derivation config and default rules; infra to prototype hot cache architecture. sync Friday.

oscar: +1. will also draft runbook for missing-envelope fallback (map to billing:unknown and emit alert).

sylvia: thanks all. I'll open a follow-up doc linking to the ingest-config PR. ping me for pairing on the proto. :wave:
